chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman whose husband divorces her, when does she have the right to dispose of herself (i.e., her waiting period is complete)? He said: 'When she sees the blood of the third menstruation, she has the right to dispose of herself.' I said: 'And if the blood comes upon her early, before the days of her qu' (waiting period)?' He said: 'If the blood comes before ten days, it is counted as hers, and it is from the menstruation from which she purified herself. And if the blood comes after ten days, it is from the third menstruation, so she has the right to dispose of herself.'

key_terms.أَمْلَكَ بِنَفْسِهَا: has the right to dispose of herself (completing iddah)

ai.seo_question: When does a divorced woman's waiting period end according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the Shia jurisprudential ruling on the iddah of a divorced woman, emphasizing that the completion of three menstrual cycles determines her freedom to remarry. It specifically addresses the scenario of early menstruation, distinguishing between a cycle that occurs before ten days (counting as a purification cycle) and one after ten days (counting as the final third cycle), thereby resolving potential ambiguities in the timing of the waiting period.
